idiom: to bite off more than one can chew
meaning: to take on a task or responsibility that is too big to manage
literal_translation: взять на себя больше, чем можешь выполнить
example: The team bit off more than it could chew when it promised to publish three volumes in one year.
origin: Refers to an animal or person taking a bite too large to chew, so the food cannot be swallowed

wrong_meanings.meaning: to eat a very small snack between meals
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is figurative and describes overcommitment, not eating

wrong_meanings.meaning: to finish a task quickly with minimal effort
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom means the opposite: taking on more than one can handle

wrong_meanings.meaning: to share a project equally with a partner
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom is about overcommitment, not about sharing work fairly

explanation: 'To bite off more than one can chew' means to take on more responsibility than one can manage. It is common in workplace and academic discussions of overambitious plans.
